candidates.headline: OpenRouter off-boards three inference providers and pulls 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention after Dragos canary study found prompt theft
candidates.published_utc: 2026-11-22 (time UNKNOWN). Original event: Dragos research published 2026-11-19 (per DEV Community/HN write-ups); study ran July-November 2026.
candidates.latest_development: OpenRouter notice (22 Nov): off-boarded three providers (unnamed), removed 125 endpoints from ZDR eligibility (flagged ones plus precautionary), notified potentially affected customers; says no breach of OpenRouter itself; ZDR reportedly default for new accounts; links notices from Novita, Phala, Together AI without saying they are the three.
candidates.public_discussion: UNKNOWN - x.com/reddit/youtube/instagram not reachable; no engagement numbers observed. Only signal: multiple outlets covering it in search results. A Digg thread on the Dragos post appeared in search results (not opened).
candidates.why_it_matters: Developers and apps that route prompts through AI routers assumed 'zero data retention' meant private; Dragos found attackers inside at least three inference providers and resellers able to read prompts. Shows the hidden supply chain behind 'which model answered you'.
candidates.audience_relevance: Developers, founders, anyone building on cheap third-party model APIs; general users of AI apps built on routers.
candidates.practical_usefulness: Actionable: check routing settings, turn on ZDR, choose first-party providers for sensitive data, avoid reseller marketplaces, rotate keys (Dragos recommendations per secondary coverage). Price: N/A.
candidates.visual_potential: Good: diagram of prompt -> router -> provider -> leak; canary token concept; screenshot of notice (if creator can open it).
candidates.verification_status: INDEPENDENTLY REPORTED (OpenRouter notice and Dragos post seen only via search index; multiple outlets: The Hacker News, Unite.AI, Brandefense, mlq.ai, DEV)
candidates.controversy: Whether 'breach' vs 'logging/retention violation' - framing contested; providers not named; Chinese-lab exfiltration detail varies across outlets.

extraordinary.who_claimed: Dragos (research, HD Moore reportedly lead per World Today News headline) and OpenRouter (action)
extraordinary.demonstrated: ~2 million canary-seeded prompts; canary AWS keys reused by attackers; at least 3 providers compromised, none had detected it (secondary coverage)
extraordinary.independent_confirmation: OpenRouter acted on findings; Together AI disclosed a separate related leak; no independent reproduction
extraordinary.uncertain: Provider identities; exact numbers (routes traced, Chinese-lab share); whether OpenRouter's 3 = Dragos's 3
extraordinary.preliminary: Partly - figures from a single research firm

candidates.window_status_v71: IN WINDOW: OpenRouter notice dated 22 Nov 2026 (time UNKNOWN); follow-up coverage 22 Nov (Phala notice details, MiniMax reseller email).
candidates.latest_development_v71: No new OpenRouter or Dragos statement found after 14:00Z.
